content:
In macOS 27「金門橋」中，Apple has put more effort into fixing bugs and improving performance. And in the beta version, the quality of life improvement I'm most looking forward to is the fix for Messages when logging into Mac.

When logging into Mac in macOS「金門橋」, Messages should already be up to date and synced.

One of Mac's biggest selling points compared to PC is how seamlessly it works with iPhone.

Features like Universal Clipboard, iPhone Mirroring, and Handoff make the collaboration between iPhone and Mac feel seamless.

But there's one area where macOS has always struggled to provide a truly seamless continuity experience: after you first log in, Messages will briefly appear unsynced.

We've all experienced this. After logging into Mac, Messages notifications immediately pop up in the top right corner of the screen, but these are messages you've already read.

However, in macOS「金門橋」, as part of its improvements to performance and refinement, Apple has significantly improved the syncing performance of Messages across different devices.

Apple says the syncing process is now more efficient. When your Mac comes online, the unread message count will be more accurate immediately, and you won't receive notifications for messages you've already read.

I use iPad Pro as my primary computer, so Mac is just a secondary device for me. Messages syncing between iPhone and iPad has almost never had issues, so the relatively poor experience Mac has always provided bothered me quite a bit.

Now, with macOS「金門橋」, this annoyance should become history. At least in the betas so far, Apple seems to have actually delivered.

How is Messages syncing performing for you in the macOS「金門橋」beta? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
